# Agent Drive quickstart

Agent Drive stores encrypted file contents for agents. The service sees paths, sizes, tags, and
activity metadata, but not plaintext file contents or drive keys. Lost drive keys cannot be recovered.

## Connect an agent

1. Create a human account at `/sign-up`.
2. Give your agent this one line, with your own origin: `Set up Agent Drive: https://agentdrive.xyz/llms.txt`.
   The agent follows the setup guide at that URL. Or do the same steps yourself, below.
3. Install the CLI (Node 20 or newer). The CLI is served by this site as a tarball:

```sh
npm install -g https://agentdrive.xyz/cli/agent-drive.tgz
# No global installs allowed? Prefix every command with:
#   npx -y https://agentdrive.xyz/cli/agent-drive.tgz
```

4. Log in. The CLI prints a link and a code.

```sh
agent-drive login --name "my agent"
# On a self-hosted installation, install from its origin and pass its API URL:
#   agent-drive login --name "my agent" --api https://YOUR-ORIGIN/api
```

5. Approve it. Open the link while signed in, check that the code matches the one the CLI printed,
   and click Approve. The command finishes by itself. You do not copy an API key.
6. Back up the credentials. The drive key exists only on this machine, so if the machine or sandbox
   is deleted the files can never be opened again.

```sh
agent-drive credentials export --to /a/path/that/survives
# or, into a secret store:
agent-drive credentials export --stdout | gh secret set AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS && agent-drive credentials confirm
```

7. Check that it worked. Setup is complete only when this prints `check ok`.

```sh
agent-drive check
```

8. Store and fetch a file, then share it.

```sh
printf 'hello from an agent\n' > sample.txt
agent-drive put ./sample.txt /sample.txt
agent-drive get /sample.txt --output ./downloaded.txt
cmp ./sample.txt ./downloaded.txt
agent-drive share /sample.txt --expires-in 24h
```

The complete share URL is a bearer secret: its fragment contains the file decryption key. Add
`--drive ID` to a command if you have more than one drive. See the [CLI reference](cli.md).

## Use MCP

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add agent-drive -- agent-drive mcp
```

Other MCP clients launch the command `agent-drive` with the argument `mcp`. Codex needs per-tool
approval for tools that change data; see the [CLI reference](cli.md). Restart the MCP client after
changing saved credentials.

## Sandboxes and more agents

- In a sandbox that is deleted or recreated, set `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` as a secret on the
  platform, using the output of `agent-drive credentials export --stdout`. Every new sandbox is then
  already connected.
- To add another agent, run `agent-drive login` on its machine and approve it in the browser. You can
  make it read-only or limit its writes to one folder.

## Operate the workspace

- The console browses metadata while locked. Load a recovery key to decrypt downloads in browser
  memory. Refreshing or leaving the files page loses that in-memory key.
- Overwrites and restores of an older version create new versions. Restoring a file's current version
  from the trash only brings it back, with no new version. Trash does not reclaim retained storage.
- Revoke an agent or API key in the console when its access is no longer required.
- `/console/billing` shows plan allowances, usage, spending controls, and statements. See
  `/pricing` for plans.
- `/console/settings` shows the account-scoped audit log and permanent deletion controls.
  Deletion requires an exact confirmation, disables new access, and queues a background purge.
  Wait for completion; accepting the request does not prove all bytes have already been erased.

# Agent Drive CLI

The CLI keeps the API token and drive keys in
`~/.config/agent-drive/config.json` (or `AGENT_DRIVE_CONFIG`). The directory is mode `0700` and
the file is mode `0600`; updates are atomic. `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL` and `AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY`
override saved values. Run `agent-drive login` with those environment variables, or pipe a token
to `agent-drive login --api URL --token-stdin`; tokens are never required in command arguments.

Drive-key precedence is the per-drive `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>` variable (uppercase, with
non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `_`), then `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY`, then `--key-file`, then the
locally saved key. Drive keys are client secrets and are never sent to the API or S3.

Commands include `login`, `whoami`, `agent create`, `drive create`, `check`, `key create`, `key revoke`,
`put`, `get`, `ls`, `mv`, `cp`, `rm`, `versions`, `restore`, `search`, `recent`, and `sync`.
`put LOCAL REMOTE --drive ID` is create-only by default and encrypts before requesting an upload URL.
A conflict prints what to do: `exists` and `changed` print "Current version: ID. Read the file again, merge
your change, then retry with --if-version ID."; `trashed` says to restore the file or write with `--overwrite`;
`absent` says to write without `--if-version`.
Use `--overwrite` for an unconditional replacement, or `--if-version ID` for an optimistic
conditional replacement; these flags are mutually exclusive. `get REMOTE --drive ID
--output FILE` writes only after authenticated decryption succeeds; without `--output`, only
small valid UTF-8 files are printed. No CLI or MCP output shows the presigned download URL or the wrapped file key (`downloadUrl`, `wrappedKey`); versions print id, path, size, author and timestamps.
Every drive command defaults `--drive` to the only drive key saved for the current API origin; with none or several it fails and lists the configured ids.
Inline text output rejects binary control bytes while allowing tabs and line breaks. `ls` and
`search` accept `--agent`, `--machine`, `--user`, and `--tag`. `ls --folder PATH` lists that folder's immediate children as files and folder rows (`kind`, `items`, `ciphertextSize`, `createdAt`), and `ls --sort modified` lists newest first (`--sort path` is the default; `--folder` and `--prefix` cannot be combined). The MCP `list` tool takes the same optional `folder` and `sort` parameters. Without them `ls` and `list` behave as before; `recent` accepts `--since`, `--cursor`, and `--wait SECONDS` (1 to 300; polls every 2 seconds for the next event, one metered operation per poll).

Drive creation is idempotent. A newly created drive generates and prints a key once with a backup
warning. Re-running against an existing drive uses the retained local key and refuses to invent a
replacement when the backup is missing. Creating a scoped API key remains an explicit `key create`
step; a management key is not silently granted drive access.

`sync LOCAL_DIRECTORY --drive ID --prefix /folder` is upload-only. It skips symlinks, never
deletes remote files, stores private SHA-256/version manifests outside the uploaded directory,
skips unchanged files, and refuses unknown remote files unless `--overwrite-existing` is supplied
for deliberate initial adoption. That flag still uses a current-version guard; files with existing
manifest history always conflict if their remote version changed. It reads each local file once and
hashes the exact bytes uploaded. Corrupt or unreadable manifests fail rather than resetting conflict
history. Sync state is stored in a private sibling directory named `<config-path>.state`; an
existing state directory with unsafe permissions is rejected without changing its mode. Config
updates use an exclusive `<config-path>.lock` directory. A crashed CLI may leave that lock; remove
it manually only after confirming no Agent Drive CLI process is active. It is not a download or
destructive mirror.

## Install, device login, and backup

Install from the site: `npm install -g https://agentdrive.xyz/cli/agent-drive.tgz`, or run
without installing: `npx -y https://agentdrive.xyz/cli/agent-drive.tgz <command>`. The
Vercel build packs `packages/agent-drive` into `apps/web/public/cli/agent-drive.tgz`. The default
API URL is `https://agentdrive.xyz/api` (override with `--api` or `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL`).

`agent-drive login [--name AGENT] [--no-browser]` runs the OAuth device flow when no
`AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY` or `--token-stdin` is given. It prints a link and a code, opens a browser only
when stdout is a TTY, `CI` is unset, and `--no-browser` is absent, then polls until the human
approves. The default name is `<machine> agent`. It sends the saved drive IDs for the same API origin
as `known_drive_ids`, saves the API key and unsealed drive keys to the private config, and never
prints them. A drive key that fails to unseal is reported and skipped. If no granted drive has a
usable key, login exits 1 (the config is still saved); run `login` again. Otherwise it prints the
usable drives and the config path.

`agent-drive whoami` adds `localDriveKeys`, a map of authorized drive IDs to whether this machine
holds a key. `agent-drive check [--drive ID]` first downloads the newest existing file (other than
the check file) and fails with "This drive key cannot decrypt existing files." if the key cannot
open it. Then it writes a random file to `/.agent-drive/check.txt` (under the key's first write path, if it has any) with overwrite, reads it back, and prints `check ok drive=<id>`, or fails with exit 1. A key without the `write` scope cannot write, so `check` lists live files, downloads and decrypts the first one that still exists, and prints `check ok drive=<id> (read-only)` without writing anything. If no file decrypts (an empty drive), it prints `check not verified drive=<id>: ...` and exits 1; run it again after another agent writes a file. `drive create`
prints only the drive and a note on stderr that the key is saved to the config; it never prints the
key. A `permission_denied` error about a missing scope adds a hint to run `agent-drive login` again.

`key create --agent ID --drive ID --label L --scope read --scope write [--write-path /inbox/x]...` limits the key's writes, moves, copies, deletes and restores to those folders (up to 16; each a canonical absolute path). Reads stay drive-wide. `whoami` shows `writePaths` (empty means no limit).

## Credential backup and skill install (contract section 9)

The drive key lives only in the config file, so lose the machine and the files cannot be opened.

- `agent-drive credentials export (--to PATH [--force] | --stdout)` writes a bundle:
  `adcred1.` plus base64url of `{"v":1,"apiUrl","apiKey","driveKeys","driveKeyOrigins"}`. `--to`
  writes a mode `0600` file and refuses an existing path without `--force`. `--stdout` prints only
  when stdout is not a terminal (pipe it to a secret store), waits for stdout to drain, and fails on
  EPIPE. `--to` and `skill install` write through a temp file and rename, and refuse a symlink
  destination. The bundle is the only secret the CLI
  ever prints. A `--to` export records `keyBackup: { "<driveId>": { at, method } }` in the config and
  then calls `POST /v1/drives/:id/key-backup` with `{ method }` for each drive; a failed call is
  only a warning. A `--stdout` export records nothing; run
  `agent-drive credentials export --stdout | <secret store> && agent-drive credentials confirm`
  (`confirm [--method stdout]` records the backup and reports it). Use `set -o pipefail` so a failed
  store stops `confirm`. A login that replaces the API key clears all backup records (the exported
  bundle holds the revoked key) and says so; `check` then asks for a new export.
- `agent-drive credentials issue --name NAME [--drive ID] [--scope S]... [--write-path P]... [--label L] (--to PATH [--force] | --stdout)`
  needs the `delegate` scope. It creates a new agent `NAME` with its own API key (default scopes
  `read write`, which must be within the caller's own; the drive defaults to the only configured
  drive key) and prints one `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS=adcred1.…` line holding only that key and the
  chosen drive's key. The caller's own API key and config are neither included nor changed. `--to`
  and `--stdout` follow the same terminal and mode `0600` rules as `export`. Store the line as a
  secret in the sandbox. A name that already exists returns 409; pick another. Revoke the issued
  key alone from the console under Agents.
- `agent-drive grant CODE [--drive ID] [--read-only] [--scope S]... [--write-path P]...` needs the
  `delegate` scope. `CODE` is the code a new agent's `agent-drive login` showed. It prints
  `Request from <client_name> on <machine>, made <time>.`, seals this machine's drive key to the
  login's public key (the `adk-device-v1` sealed-key format), posts the sealed
  blob as an offer, and prints `Offered drive <id> to <name> (<scopes>; writes under <paths>). The
owner approves at <origin>/connect?code=CODE.` It does not approve: the human opens that page and
  clicks Approve once. The drive defaults to the only configured drive key. Scopes default to
  `read write` (`read` with `--read-only`); they must be within the caller's own, else pass
  `--scope`. Write paths default to the caller's own. It never prints or sends a key in the clear. It offers only a drive key saved for the current API origin (as login does); a key from `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY*`, `--key-file`, or saved for another origin is refused, so an endpoint other than the key's own cannot obtain it.
  Which handoff when: `grant` when the new agent has a shell and a human is present; the human opens
  Details on `/connect` and chooses "Use one of my drives instead" when they hold the recovery file; `credentials
issue` for a sandbox with no browser.
- `agent-drive credentials import [--from PATH]` merges a bundle (file or stdin) into the config
  and marks its drives as backed up.
- `agent-drive credentials status` prints, per drive key, whether and when it was backed up.
- `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS=<bundle>` is merged in memory at startup and never written to disk. The
  saved config and the explicit variables (`AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL`, `AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY`,
  `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<ID>`) take precedence over it. Its drives count as backed up (method `env`)
  and are reported once per process, but only for drives whose effective key (after the precedence
  above) equals the bundle's key and whose recorded origin matches the API origin.
- `login` and `drive create` print the backup instructions when they create a drive key.
  `check` fails with "drive key not backed up" until every usable key is backed up (a key supplied
  by `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY*` or `--key-file` is already outside the config and is exempt). `whoami`
  includes `keyBackup`.
- `agent-drive skill install [--target claude|codex|DIR]` copies the packaged `SKILL.md` to
  `~/.claude/skills/agent-drive/` and `~/.codex/skills/agent-drive/` when those directories exist
  (or to the target), and prints the paths written. With none found it prints the packaged file's
  location. It writes into the agent's own skills folder, so in a sandbox, CI or on a shared machine use `--target DIR` or skip it.

On reconnect, `login` sends the saved API key as a bearer header only when the saved API URL has the
same origin as the login URL. The config records each drive key's origin in `driveKeyOrigins`. Keys
with a different or unknown origin, or that do not decode to 32 bytes, are not sent or counted as
usable. Configs written before origins were recorded are migrated when read: a drive key with no
origin is assigned the origin of the saved `apiUrl` (and kept only if one is saved); the migration is
written back on the next config write. The default agent name is `<machine> agent`, truncated to 64 characters.

`agent-drive backup LOCAL_DIRECTORY [--drive ID] [--prefix PATH] [--dry-run]` uploads every regular
file to `PATH/<relative path>` (default `/backups/<machine>`) with overwrite, so history is kept.
The drive defaults to the only drive key in config. A private manifest in `<config-path>.state`,
keyed by server, drive, prefix, and relative path, lets later runs skip unchanged files by SHA-256.
Symlinks are skipped, and one failing file does not stop the rest. It prints
`backup uploaded=N unchanged=N failed=N` and exits 1 if any file failed.

## Capture

`agent-drive capture [--drive ID] [--agent NAME] -- COMMAND [ARGS...]` runs COMMAND with a local proxy on
`127.0.0.1` (random port) and sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/anthropic` and
`OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openai` in the child's environment only. Requests are forwarded
unchanged to `api.anthropic.com` or `api.openai.com` and streamed back as they arrive. A redacted copy of
each exchange is encrypted with the drive key and saved to
`/traces/<agent>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS.mmm>Z_<model>_<id>.json` with the tags `trace`, `agent:<agent>` and
`model:<model>`. `--agent` defaults to the command's basename (lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`;
at most 40 characters). The command's exit code is passed through.

**What is captured.** HTTP calls to the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs made by an agent that honors the base-URL
variables, such as `claude` and `codex` in API-key mode. Each file holds the method, path, an allowlisted set
of headers (no `authorization`, `x-api-key`, cookies or any other header), and the request and response
bodies. Streaming responses are stored as a list of SSE events. Each body is cut at 4 MiB and each file is kept
under 9 MiB; cut parts are named in the `truncated` list. Everything you send to the model, including any secrets you paste into a prompt, is saved in the trace, encrypted with your drive key. Values of query parameters whose names look like credentials (`key`, `token`, `secret`, `auth`, `signature`) are replaced with `[redacted]`, and request URLs are never printed with their query string.

**What is not captured.** The Claude desktop app and editor extensions, other traffic from the agent (updates,
telemetry), Codex websocket transport, Codex ChatGPT-login mode, and agents already pointed at another gateway.

**When COMMAND runs unwrapped.** The agent always runs. If capture cannot start (no saved API credentials, no
drive key, the port or spool directory is unavailable), or the agent already has a provider configured
(`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` for `claude`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` or a `-c model_provider`, `-c model_providers.*`,
`--config` or `--profile`/`-p` argument for `codex`, either variable for other commands), the CLI prints one
`capture disabled: <reason>; running <command> without capture` line and runs COMMAND with its environment and
arguments unchanged. Nothing in a shell profile, Claude settings or `~/.codex/config.toml` is ever written.

**Codex flags.** For a command named `codex`, these are added before your arguments:
`-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.name="Agent Drive capture"`,
`-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.base_url="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openai/v1"`,
`-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.env_key="OPENAI_API_KEY"`,
`-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.wire_api="responses"`,
`-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.supports_websockets=false` and
`-c model_provider="agent_drive_capture"`.

**Spool.** Encrypted traces are written to `<config-path>.state/capture/<driveId>/` (directory mode 0700, files
0600; ciphertext plus a small JSON sidecar, never plaintext) and uploaded in the background with create-only
writes. The spool holds at most about 512 MiB (the cap is approximate when several capture processes share a spool); past that, new traces are not saved and are counted as
`spool full`. Traces that cannot be uploaded (offline, 5xx, 429) stay and are retried on a later run; a stop
condition (invalid key, no permission, no quota) leaves them for the next run, and traces the server rejects
as invalid are moved to `invalid/`. Each request is also logged to stderr as
`capture: <METHOD> <path> <status> <ms>ms <captured | not captured: reason>`.

At exit the CLI waits up to 5 s for pending captures and 10 s in total for uploads, then prints
`capture: <uploaded> uploaded, <queued> queued (<MiB> MiB in <spool dir>), <dropped> not captured (<reasons>), <invalid> invalid`.

## MCP server

Traces that arrive through the OpenRouter webhook are sealed to the drive's trace inbox rather than to the drive key. `get`, `download` and `share` open them with the same drive key: the client fetches the drive's inbox record once per process and unwraps the inbox private key locally. The MCP `get` tool returns at most 64 KiB inline, and traces are often larger, so use `download` for large traces.

`agent-drive mcp` serves `whoami`, `put`, `get` (inline text up to 64 KiB, read-only), `download` (writes a new local file at `outputPath`, never overwrites), `list`, `move`, `copy`, `delete`, `versions`,
`restore`, `search`, `recent` and `share`. `driveId` is optional: it defaults to the only drive key
saved for the current API origin (same rule as the CLI's `--drive`); with several, the error lists
the configured IDs. Tools carry MCP annotations. `whoami`, `get`, `list`, `versions`, `search` and
`recent` have `readOnlyHint: true`. `put`, `move`, `delete` and `restore` have `readOnlyHint: false`
and `destructiveHint: true`; `copy`, `share` and `download` have `readOnlyHint: false` and
`destructiveHint: false`.

Codex asks for approval before any tool that is not read-only. Under `codex exec` the approval
policy is `never`, so the call fails with "MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is
never". Approve the tools the agent needs, one by one, in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.agent-drive]
command = "agent-drive"
args = ["mcp"]
[mcp_servers.agent-drive.tools.put]
approval_mode = "approve"
[mcp_servers.agent-drive.tools.download]
approval_mode = "approve"
```

`default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"` under the server approves every tool, including `delete`,
`move`, `restore` and `share`; use it only as an explicit opt-in.
Verified with codex-cli 0.166.0 (`gpt-6-luna`, `--sandbox workspace-write`): `put` and `get`
completed with `default_tools_approval_mode="approve"`, and `put` passed approval with
`tools.put.approval_mode="approve"`. `download` was not run under Codex.

# Phase 1 API contract

The typed route inventory is exported from `apps/web/src/api/contract.ts`. Every request uses a
bearer API key; successful JSON responses and errors are `Cache-Control: no-store`. Errors use
`{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`.

## Routes

| Method   | Route                                                                | Required scope                      |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| GET      | `/api/v1/whoami`                                                     | authenticated                       |
| GET/POST | `/api/v1/agents`                                                     | `manage`                            |
| GET/POST | `/api/v1/drives`                                                     | read/manage; POST requires `manage` |
| GET/POST | `/api/v1/keys`                                                       | `manage`                            |
| DELETE   | `/api/v1/keys/:id`                                                   | `manage`                            |
| GET      | `/api/v1/device/:code`                                               | `delegate`                          |
| POST     | `/api/v1/device/:code/grant`                                         | `delegate`                          |
| POST     | `/api/v1/drives/:id/put`                                             | `write`                             |
| POST     | `/api/v1/drives/:id/commit`                                          | `write`                             |
| GET      | `/api/v1/drives/:id/get`, `/list`, `/versions`, `/recent`, `/search` | `read`                              |
| GET      | `/api/v1/drives/:id/trace-inbox`                                     | `read`                              |
| POST     | `/api/v1/drives/:id/key-backup`                                      | `write`                             |
| POST     | `/api/v1/drives/:id/move`                                            | `write`                             |
| POST     | `/api/v1/drives/:id/delete`                                          | `delete`                            |
| POST     | `/api/v1/drives/:id/copy`, `/restore`                                | `read` and `write`                  |

All collection endpoints return `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor": string | null }`. Pass `limit`
(default 50, maximum 100) and the returned opaque `nextCursor` to continue. Ordering is stable
within a collection; cursors are validated and should be treated as opaque. `GET /drives` lists all
account drives for management keys and only key-authorized drives for keys with `read`. `whoami`
returns identity, scopes, and authorized drive IDs (`null` for management keys); use the paginated
drives endpoint for names and quota details. It also reports `egressMeteringConfigured` (whether
access-log based egress measurement is configured) and `egressNotMetered` (whether the provider
does not charge for egress). The usage endpoint reports these fields alongside `egressBytes`, which
is `null` when access-log measurement is not configured.

File `list` and `search` accept `agentId`, `machine`, and `user` filters; `list` also accepts a
literal path `prefix` and optional path query `q`. `%` and `_` in a prefix are treated literally.

`list` also accepts two optional parameters. Without them the response is unchanged. `sort=modified`
orders newest first by the current version's `created_at` (default `sort=path`). `delimiter=/`
returns the immediate children of `prefix` (the root when empty): file rows carry `kind: "file"`
plus the usual fields, and folder rows are `{ kind: "folder", path, items, ciphertext_size,
created_at }`, where `items` is the number of direct children, `ciphertext_size` is the sum of the
current versions below the folder, and `created_at` is the newest of them. Filters apply to files
before grouping. Cursors from one sort or mode are rejected by another with `validation_error`. Any
other `sort` or `delimiter` value is a `validation_error`.
`versions`, `recent`, and `search` use the same bounded pagination envelope as other collections.
A conditional `put` (`ifVersionId`, or `ifVersionId: null` for create-only) that loses returns 409 `conflict`
with `state` (`exists`, `changed`, `trashed`, or `absent`) and `currentVersionId` (the current or trashed
version id; `null` for `absent`). A conditional write never revives a trashed file; an unconditional
overwrite does.

`restore` with no `versionId`, or with the file's current version, undeletes a trashed file: it returns the existing version with 200, creates no version or copy, and does not check quota; on a live file it does nothing. Restoring any other version copies it as a new current version and returns 201.

`recent` returns file-operation events (`put`, `copy`, `restore`, `move`, `delete`) in commit
order, except events written before the 2026 ordering change (migration 0015), which are ordered by creation time instead. Pass the `latestCursor` from one response as `cursor` to get only newer events; with a
cursor the order is exact and `since` is ignored. Without a cursor, the optional exclusive `since`
timestamp compares with the transaction start time, so it is approximate. `latestCursor` is the last
item's cursor, or the request cursor when there are no new events (`null` if none). Cursors from
before this ordering existed are rejected with 400. Each event includes the current
`path`, `previousPath` for moves, version and actor IDs, the author's `agentName` (null if the
agent was removed), and `createdAt`; each poll counts as one `drive.recent` operation; it never includes object
keys, wrapped keys, or signed URLs. Move and delete accept an optional `userId` in the request body;
the machine actor is taken from `x-agent-drive-machine`.

Production API requests must use HTTPS based on the request URL protocol; forwarded headers cannot
override this check. HTTP is allowed in local and test environments.

Audit entries contain the authenticated key/account/agent IDs, fixed route action, outcome, safe
error code, and HTTP status. They omit bodies, tokens, wrapped keys, object URLs, and paths. If the
audit write fails, the API returns 500; a mutation may already have committed before that response.

## Drive key backup status

`POST /api/v1/drives/:id/key-backup` with `{ "method": "file" | "stdout" | "env" }` records that the
drive's key has been backed up outside the machine. It requires the `write` scope on that drive; the
console session may also call it as `/api/console/drives/:id/key-backup`. It returns
`200 { keyBackupAt, keyBackupMethod }` and writes the audit action `drive.key_backup`. Unknown fields
and other methods return 400, so key material is never accepted. A drive of another account, or one
outside the key's drives, returns 404. `GET /drives` includes `key_backup_at` and `key_backup_method`
(both null until reported).

## Device authorization (agent login)

These endpoints use no API key.

- `POST /api/oauth/device_authorization` with `client_name`, `machine` (optional), `public_key`,
  optional `known_drive_ids` (up to 20 UUIDs; JSON array, or repeated or comma-separated form
  field; invalid input returns 400 `invalid_request`), and an optional `Authorization: Bearer`
  header with the CLI's current key (ignored if invalid or revoked). `known_drive_ids` count only
  with that key: reconnect drives are the ids that key holds. Returns `device_code`, `user_code`, `verification_uri`,
  `verification_uri_complete`, `expires_in` (600), and `interval` (5). At most 20 starts per IP
  per hour; the 21st returns 429 `{"error":"slow_down"}`.
- `POST /api/oauth/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` and
  `device_code`. Errors are 400 `{"error": …}`: `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`,
  `access_denied`, `expired_token`, `invalid_grant`, `unsupported_grant_type`. On approval it
  returns the API key once, with `scope`, `api_url`, `account_id`, `agent_id`, `agent_name`,
  `drive_ids`, `new_drive_id`, and `sealed_drive_keys`.
- Console (Clerk session): `GET /api/console/device/{user_code}`,
  `POST /api/console/device/{user_code}/approve`, and `POST /api/console/device/{user_code}/deny`.
  The lookup also returns `drives` (`[{id, name}]`, the requested drives that still belong to the
  account) and `creates_drive`. Approving with `{}` grants read, write, delete, and share on those
  drives, or on a new drive named after the agent (`name`, `name (machine)`, `name 2`, ...;
  drives pending deletion keep their names). Token issuance revokes exactly the bearer key sent at
  start, if it belongs to the same account and agent. Defaults apply only to an empty body.
  Any other body is explicit approval: `scopes` (required, never `manage`), `driveIds`,
  `newDriveName`, optional `agentId`, and optional `sealedDriveKeys`. A `newDriveName` that matches an existing drive returns 409. Each
  account gets 30 device calls and 10 `not_found` results per 10 minutes; beyond that, 429
  `rate_limited`. Revoking an agent denies its approved but unredeemed requests.
- A key missing a scope gets 403 `permission_denied`: `The API key lacks the "<scope>" scope.`
- Grant by an existing agent (delegation). `GET /api/v1/device/:code` with a `delegate` key returns `{ user_code, client_name, machine, created_at, expires_at, public_key }` for a pending, unexpired request, else 404. `POST /api/v1/device/:code/grant` with `{ driveId, scopes, writePaths, sealedDriveKey: { epk, iv, ct } }` records an offer for the caller's account and returns `{ status: 'offered', revision }`; a repeat replaces the offer and raises the revision. It must pass `assertDelegation` (403). It does not approve: the human approves on `/connect`. Both routes share the console device-code budget per account: 30 calls, and 10 `not_found` results, per 10 minutes; past either, 429 `rate_limited`. Audit actions `device.read` and `device.grant`. The console `GET /device/:code` also returns `offer` and `offerRevision`; the approve body carries `offerRevision`, and a stale one returns 409 `The request changed; reload the page.`
- A key with `writePaths` (`POST /api/v1/keys` and the approve body accept `writePaths`: at most 16 canonical absolute paths, not `/`; `GET /keys` returns `write_paths`; `whoami` returns `writePaths`) may only put, move, copy, delete and restore at or under those paths, else 403 `permission_denied`: `The API key may only write under <paths>.` An empty list means no limit. Reads are not limited. The console is not affected.
- Delegated `POST /api/v1/keys`: a key that holds `delegate` but not `manage` may call it with `agentName` (1 to 64 characters) instead of `agentId`, plus `label`, `driveIds`, `scopes` and optional `writePaths`. The request must pass `assertDelegation` (403 `A key cannot grant more than it holds.`; 403 naming the scope without `delegate`). The server always creates a new agent of that name; an existing name returns 409 `conflict`: `An agent named "<name>" already exists; choose another name.` `agentId` from such a caller returns 400. The key records `issued_by_agent_id` (the caller's agent), which `GET /keys` returns. `DELETE /keys/:id` (a `manage` call) revokes the issued key alone; revoking the issuer does not cascade. Audit action stays `keys.create`.
- Audit actions: `device.authorize`, `device.token`, `console.device.read`,
  `console.device.approve`, `console.device.deny`.

## Account key (passphrase unlock, console only)

Clerk-session routes under `/api/console/`. There are no bearer routes: agents, the CLI and MCP
never see the public key, the wrapped private key or slots. The server stores opaque records and
checks structure and size only. It never receives a passphrase, KEK, private key, drive key or
plaintext. Slots are not backups and never touch `key_backup_at` / `key_backup_method`.

**strict** routes need a recent Clerk `strict` reverification. When it is missing they return
exactly Clerk's `reverificationErrorResponse('strict')` (403) so `useReverification` can recover.
`DELETE /api/console/account` is now **strict** too. Test auth always counts as reverified.

| Route                                 | Body, response                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Audit action                       |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `GET /account-key`                    | `{ accountKey: { id, accountId, format, publicKey, wrappedPrivateKey, wrapGeneration, kdf: { name, iterations, salt }, createdAt, updatedAt } \| null }`                                                                                                   | `console.account_key.read`         |
| `POST /account-key` (**strict**)      | `{ id, publicKey, wrappedPrivateKey, kdf }` returns 201 with the record. 409 if one exists.                                                                                                                                                                | `console.account_key.create`       |
| `PATCH /account-key` (**strict**)     | `{ expectedKeyId, expectedGeneration, wrappedPrivateKey, kdf }` returns the record with `wrapGeneration + 1`. 409 unless both match; 404 if none.                                                                                                          | `console.account_key.update`       |
| `DELETE /account-key` (**strict**)    | `{ expectedKeyId, confirmation: "RESET" }` returns `{ deletedSlots }`. 409 if the id is not current; 404 if none.                                                                                                                                          | `console.account_key.reset`        |
| `GET /account-key/slots?limit&cursor` | `{ items: [{ driveId, keyId, format, sealed, revision }], nextCursor }` for live drives, ordered by drive id                                                                                                                                               | `console.account_key.slots`        |
| `POST /drives/:id/account-key`        | `{ keyId, expectedRevision: number \| null, sealed: { epk, iv, ct } }` returns `{ revision }`. `null` creates (409 if a slot exists); a number replaces that revision (409 otherwise). 409 if `keyId` is not current; 404 for a foreign or deleting drive. | `console.drive.account_key.put`    |
| `DELETE /drives/:id/account-key`      | `{ keyId, expectedRevision }` returns `{ deleted: true }`. 409 on a stale key or revision; 404 if no slot.                                                                                                                                                 | `console.drive.account_key.delete` |

Validation: unknown fields are 400. All base64url values are canonical and unpadded. `publicKey` and
`sealed.epk` are 65 bytes starting with `0x04`; `kdf.name` is `PBKDF2-SHA256`; `kdf.iterations` is an
integer from 600000 to 2000000; `kdf.salt` is 16 bytes; `wrappedPrivateKey` is `0x01 || iv(12) ||
ciphertext+tag` of 1+12+16+32..256 bytes; `sealed.iv` is 12 bytes and `sealed.ct` is 59 bytes.

Writes lock the account row (shared, `deleting_at` must be null, else 409), then the account key
row, then for slot routes the drive row (`deleting_at` must be null, else 404). Drive deletion
removes the drive's slot; account deletion removes the account key (slots cascade).

## Trace inbox and webhook token

A drive can hold one trace inbox: an ECDH public key plus its private key wrapped by the client
with the drive key, so the server can store it but not open it. A drive can also hold one active
webhook token. Console routes need a Clerk session and the same-origin check; they are not
reverification-gated because they reveal or change no key the server can use. A bearer key can
only read the inbox. Every other route below returns 404 on `/api/v1`.

| Route                              | Body, response                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Audit action                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `GET /drives/:id/trace-inbox`      | `{ inbox: { keyId, publicKey, wrappedPrivateKey, createdAt } \| null }`. On `/api/v1` the key needs `read` on the drive; counts as one operation like `get`.                                                                               | `drive.trace_inbox.read`             |
| `POST /drives/:id/trace-inbox`     | Console only. `{ keyId, publicKey, wrappedPrivateKey }` returns 201 with the same shape. 409 if the drive already has an inbox. Unknown fields are 400.                                                                                    | `console.drive.trace_inbox.create`   |
| `GET /drives/:id/webhook-token`    | Console only. `{ token: { id, createdAt } \| null }`. Never the secret or its hash.                                                                                                                                                        | `console.drive.webhook_token.read`   |
| `POST /drives/:id/webhook-token`   | Console only. Returns 201 `{ id, token, url, createdAt }`; `token` is `adw_` plus 64 hex characters and is shown once (only its SHA-256 is stored). Revokes the active token in the same transaction. 409 if the drive has no trace inbox. | `console.drive.webhook_token.create` |
| `DELETE /drives/:id/webhook-token` | Console only. Revokes the active token and returns `{ revokedAt }`; 404 if none is active.                                                                                                                                                 | `console.drive.webhook_token.revoke` |

Tokens belong to the account's `openrouter` agent, which is created on first use. Deleting a drive
removes its inbox and tokens.

### OpenRouter webhook

`POST /api/webhooks/openrouter/:driveId` (not under `/api/v1`; auth is the drive's webhook token as
`Authorization: Bearer adw_...`). HTTPS only in production (403 otherwise). The body is OTLP JSON,
at most 4 MiB (413 `validation_error`). The token is checked first: a missing, wrong, revoked or
other-drive token is 401, even with `X-Test-Connection`. After that:

| Case                                | Response                                                        |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `X-Test-Connection` header          | 200 `{ ok: true }`, nothing stored or charged                   |
| Not a JSON object, or no spans      | 200 `{ ok: true, stored: 0 }`                                   |
| Stored                              | 201 `{ ok: true, stored: 1, path }` under `/traces/openrouter/` |
| Same body delivered again           | 200 `{ ok: true, stored: 0, duplicate: true }`                  |
| Drive has no trace inbox            | 409                                                             |
| Drive quota or plan budget exceeded | 413 `quota_exceeded` or 402, normal error body                  |

The path is a pure function of the body (earliest span start, model, SHA-256 prefix), so a retry
maps to the same path. The server sees the payload in plaintext for the length of the request, then
stores it sealed to the drive's inbox key (see `docs/crypto.md`). Audit action: `webhook.trace.ingest`.

# Client encryption format

Agent Drive client encryption uses the versioned `ADRV v1` format. The byte API buffers a
complete file in memory; authenticated chunks are an integrity format, not a constant-memory
streaming claim.

## Ciphertext layout

The first 25 bytes are the header:

| Offset | Length | Meaning                                     |
| ------ | -----: | ------------------------------------------- |
| 0      |      5 | ASCII `ADRV` followed by version byte `1`   |
| 5      |      4 | Chunk size, unsigned big-endian (`1048576`) |
| 9      |      8 | Random base nonce                           |
| 17     |      8 | Plaintext length, unsigned big-endian       |

The payload contains one AES-256-GCM frame per 1 MiB chunk. Each frame is ciphertext followed by
its 16-byte authentication tag. The nonce is the 8-byte header nonce followed by the unsigned
big-endian chunk index. The AAD is the complete 25-byte header followed by the 4-byte chunk index
and a one-byte final-frame flag (`1` only on the last frame). Empty files still contain one
authenticated empty frame.

Every file version gets a fresh random 32-byte file key and nonce. The file key is wrapped by the
32-byte drive key with AES-256-GCM and fixed AAD `agent-drive:wrapped-file-key:v1`. The 61-byte
envelope is `version(1) || nonce(12) || wrapped-file-key-and-tag(48)`, encoded as canonical
unpadded base64url (normally 82 characters). The server stores this opaque envelope but never
receives the drive key or plaintext.

The frozen vectors and tamper/isolation tests in
`packages/agent-drive/src/crypto.unit.test.ts` are permanent compatibility guards. Future
sharing and key-rotation formats must remain explicitly versioned.

## Account key v1

The console can keep an account-level key pair so one passphrase opens every drive the user has
added. The service stores only the records below. It never receives a passphrase, a KEK, the
private key or a drive key. This is separate from `ADRV v1` and the wrapped file key, which do not
change. Implementation: `apps/web/src/console/account-key.ts`. Permanent vectors:
`apps/web/src/console/account-key.vectors.ts` (unit test and a Chromium run in
`tests/e2e/account-key-vectors.spec.ts`).

All base64url is unpadded and canonical (re-encode and compare).

- **Key pair.** ECDH P-256. `publicKey` is the 65-byte raw uncompressed point (`0x04` prefix), 87
  characters. `keyId` is a client-made UUID, new at every reset.
- **KEK.** `passphrase.normalize('NFKC')` as UTF-8, no trimming. PBKDF2-SHA256, 16-byte random
  salt, iterations an integer in 600000 to 2000000 (default 600000). AES-GCM-256 key usable for
  `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` only.
- **Wrapped private key (format 1).** AAD is UTF-8
  `agent-drive:account-key:v1:{accountId}:{keyId}:{wrapGeneration}:{publicKey}`. The PKCS#8 private
  key is wrapped with AES-GCM and a random 12-byte IV. The record value is
  `base64url(0x01 || iv(12) || ciphertext||tag)`; decoded length is `1 + 12 + 16 + n`, 32 <= n <= 256.
  `wrapGeneration` starts at 1 and goes up by 1 at each passphrase change. A passphrase change
  re-wraps the same key and does not revoke an old wrapper.
- **Slot (format 1).** A drive key (43 characters) sealed with the device seal construction
  (`docs/agent-login.md` section 4) with HKDF salt `agent-drive-account-v1`, and HKDF info and
  AES-GCM AAD both equal to UTF-8 `{keyId}:{driveId}`. Stored as `{ epk, iv, ct }` with 87, 16 and
  79 characters. After unsealing, `decodeDriveKey` must accept the result. The device seal
  (salt `agent-drive-device-v1`, info and AAD = `driveId`) is unchanged.
- **Validation before crypto.** A client parses every server record (`parseAccountKeyRecord`,
  `parseSlot`) before any PBKDF2 or ECDH: format, KDF name, iteration range, canonical base64url,
  salt and IV lengths, wrapped-key length rule, UUIDs, `wrapGeneration` a positive safe integer,
  `accountId` equal to the session account, and the public key imported as a P-256 point.
- **Generated passphrase.** 20 symbols from `0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ`, each `byte & 31` of
  `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(20))` (100 bits, no modulo bias). The passphrase is the
  20 characters with no separators.
- **Display fingerprint.** First 8 bytes of SHA-256 of the raw public key, as four hex groups. It
  is for display only.

## Trace inbox v1 and wrapped-key envelope v2

A trace inbox lets the service encrypt a file for a drive without holding the drive key. Each
drive has at most one inbox: a P-256 key pair whose private key is stored wrapped under the drive
key. Anyone holding the drive key can unwrap it. Code: `packages/agent-drive/src/trace-inbox.ts`,
frozen vectors in `trace-inbox.vectors.ts`.

All base64url is unpadded and canonical.

- **Stored record.** `{ keyId, publicKey, wrappedPrivateKey, createdAt }`. `keyId` is a UUID.
  `publicKey` is the 65-byte raw uncompressed point, 87 characters. Readers add the `driveId`
  they requested before calling crypto; a `driveId` from the server record is never trusted.
- **Wrapped private key.** The PKCS#8 private key is wrapped with AES-GCM under the drive key.
  AAD is UTF-8 `agent-drive:trace-inbox:v1:{driveId}:{keyId}:{publicKey}`. The value is
  `base64url(0x01 || iv(12) || ciphertext||tag)`, decoded length `1 + 12 + 16 + n`, 32 <= n <= 256.
  Because the AAD includes `driveId`, a record copied from another drive does not unwrap.
- **Envelope v2.** `0x02 || epk(65) || iv(12) || ct(59)`, 137 bytes, 183 characters. `epk` is an
  ephemeral raw P-256 point. `ct` is the 43-character base64url file key plus a 16-byte tag. The
  key agreement is ECDH, then HKDF-SHA-256 with salt `agent-drive-trace-inbox-v1`. HKDF info and
  AES-GCM AAD are both UTF-8 `{keyId}:{driveId}:{epk}:{publicKey}`, where `epk` is the 87-character
  base64url of the envelope's ephemeral point and `publicKey` is the inbox public key. This binds
  the serialized point, so a negated or re-encoded `epk` does not open. A reader also rejects any
  `epk` whose first byte is not `0x04`. Envelope v1 (82 characters, drive-key wrapped)
  and the ADRV v1 body format are unchanged.
- **Reading.** `envelopeVersion(wrappedKey)` returns 1 or 2. `unwrapFileKey` and `decryptFile`
  take an optional `inbox` record. A v2 envelope without one fails with `inbox_key_required`.
  Every record field is validated before any key agreement.

Webhook payloads are plaintext on the server while the request is in transit. The service
encrypts the file to the inbox public key, but it never holds the drive key and cannot read
the file afterwards. `POST /api/webhooks/openrouter/:driveId` (`apps/web/src/api/trace-webhook.ts`)
is the only route that does this: it reads the OpenRouter trace once, in memory, seals it with a
random file key, wraps that key as envelope v2, and logs nothing from the body or the token.
